Nestled within the labyrinthine network of narrow alleys and lanes of Hanoi’s Old Quarter, Hang Phen Street (Phố Hàng Phèn) emerges as a quaint and charming thoroughfare, evoking the essence of traditional Thang Long life. Historically, this street was a bustling hub for vendors selling phèn chua, a crucial commodity used by local inhabitants to clarify and filter their drinking water drawn from the Red River (Sông Hồng) or deep wells.

Over time, despite the disappearance of the sparkling phèn chua crystals, the street has retained its simple and warm charm, becoming a beloved destination for both tourists and locals. Today, Hang Phen Street stands as a testament to the enduring spirit of Hanoi’s past, where visitors can meander through its narrow lanes lined with closely packed nhà ống (tube houses), their faded yellow and moss-covered lime-washed walls contrasting with the gray, askew tiled roofs.

The street’s unique identifier is a small intersection shaded by lush, ancient bàng trees, creating a serene and tranquil atmosphere. This picturesque setting is further enhanced by the tangled network of electrical wires overhead, which add to the street’s character, while the cramped sidewalks are perpetually alive with the hustle and bustle of street vendors.
